note: Docs/json only closure of series 14I. No productive code, no tests, no frontend/backend files were touched by this stage.

productiveChanges.change: $transaction([findMany, count]) replaced with Promise.all([findMany, count]) — same where/include/select/orderBy/skip/take
Hand-copied repository-level listCache pattern (Form B, 5 modules) extracted to a shared helper createRepositoryListCache<T>(ttlMs), same TTL/behavior/invalidation function names preserved
attendanceSummary stopped wrapping 2 independent reads in prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {...}); now Promise.all on the global prisma client

productiveChanges.finding: Real bug found as a side-effect of the 14I.8 timeGridCatalogCache diagnostic (Boolean("false") === true in JS)

productiveChanges.change: Silent post-save resync effect guard replaced from useRef(false) ("first run") to useRef(refresh) + compare against last synced value — fixes a false-positive extra fetch under React 18 StrictMode double-invoke
productiveChanges.finding: x3 duplicate of GET /employees/:id/time-grid, named since 14G.9, root-caused and partially closed in this stage (x3 -> x2; remaining x2 is StrictMode-only, no production cost)

bugsFixed.description: includeDetails=false query param was silently coerced to true by z.coerce.boolean() (Boolean("false") is true in JS), so GET /employees/:id/time-grid always executed the heavy branch (period novelties + timeGridCatalogCache) regardless of what the caller asked for
bugsFixed.userFacingImpact: none observed — EmployeeHoursPage.tsx already discarded the fields gated by includeDetails, so the fix only removes wasted server work, does not change any UI behavior

bugsFixed.description: GET /employees/:id/time-grid fired 3 real requests (plus GET /novelties x2) when opening the hours edit screen for an employee, instead of the expected 2 — root cause was a useRef(false) "first render" guard in EmployeeHoursPage.tsx's post-save resync effect that did not survive React 18 StrictMode's double-invoke of the same effect
bugsFixed.foundInStage: 14I.11 (root cause independent from the includeDetails bug, confirmed not fixed by 14I.9)
bugsFixed.userFacingImpact: none — reduces wasted requests from x3 to x2; the remaining x2 is StrictMode-only (development), zero cost for a real production user
bugsFixed.wasInOriginal14I1Inventory: named as a P1 candidate since 14G.9, referenced again in 14I.1 §7, but never diagnosed or closed by any prior stage

decisionsNotToChange.reason: Measured with real data (32 employees, 1 SQL statement, 0ms query-time difference between full and reduced select, 25% payload on 8 unused sub-fields only) — the chain itself is genuinely consumed by the UI (EmployeeOrgPopover.tsx, 2 of 11 org-chart filters). No over-fetch justifying a change to a Legajos-sensitive select.

No real functional impact: the only caller (EmployeeHoursPage.tsx) always discarded the embedded data even before the includeDetails fix; after the 14I.9 fix, getTimeGridCatalogs() no longer executes at all in the real application flow. Adding invalidation to a cache with no real consumer was not justified.

decisionsNotToChange.item: Controller (createTtlCache) + repository (repositoryListCache) double cache layer in hour-concepts/novelty-types/document-categories/salary-categories
decisionsNotToChange.reason: Demonstrated with a new test per module that the repository-layer cache serves any filter-free originalUrl from a single real DB read — a mechanism the controller-layer cache (keyed by exact URL) cannot replicate alone. No bug or stale-data risk forces consolidation; doing so would be 'a refactor without a bug behind it to justify it' (14I.1's own words).

decisionsNotToChange.item: Remaining x2 StrictMode duplicate on GET /employees/:id/time-grid (Effect A, initial load)
decisionsNotToChange.reason: Zero cost in production — React only double-invokes effects in development mode, never in a production build. A real user always generated exactly 1 call from that effect.
No real caller exercises the filtered branch that uses $transaction — same criterion established since 14H.5: only fix what has a real caller, verified by grep.

decisionsNotToChange.item: relationJoins expansion beyond the 5 sites already applied since 14D.6/14D.7
decisionsNotToChange.reason: Already treated surgically and with measured evidence; the one new real candidate (GET /positions main endpoint, blocked by an untested _count + relationLoadStrategy combination) requires its own dedicated benchmark stage, not a silent extension within 14I.

remainingLowPriorityDebt: timeGridCatalogCache still has no explicit invalidation — low priority, reinforced twice (14I.8, 14I.11), no real consumer today
x2 StrictMode duplicate remains on EmployeeHoursPage.tsx initial-load effect — dev-only artifact, no production cost
salaryCategories/hourConceptRules P2 $transaction remains without a real caller

clearUsersReadCache() and salaryCategoriesReadCache.clear are still not exported as named functions, unlike employees/documents/novelties/time-entries — cosmetic asymmetry, named in 14I.7 §14, not in scope of test-only stages

future monitoring of catalog volume (double-layer cache modules and employeeOrgChartSelect) if real headcount/catalog size grows beyond today's 'small closed vocabulary' — no action needed without real volume evidence
whether to push the 18 local commits to origin/main after final user review — no push executed in any stage of the series

validationsSummary.perStageValidations: npx prisma validate / npm run typecheck / npm test / npm run build green on every stage touching backend code (14I.2, 14I.3, 14I.4, 14I.9); frontend typecheck/test/build green on 14I.11; journeys (admin-config/workforce/employees) run and green on 14I.2, 14I.3, 14I.4, 14I.11, with immediate git restore of regenerated 14D/14G/14H journey reports each time

recommendation.rationale: All 6 actionable P0/P1 findings from the original 14I.1 inventory are either fixed (3 $transaction P0, 1 $transaction P1, 1 coercion bug, 1 duplicate-request bug) or closed without action backed by measured evidence (employeeOrgChartSelect, timeGridCatalogCache, double cache layer). The 2 P2 findings without a real caller remain accepted debt, consistent with the project's established criterion since 14H.5. Each successive diagnostic in the series (14I.5, 14I.8, 14I.10, 14I.11) found less new actionable work, not more — a sign of diminishing returns, not unfinished work.
